harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up automated one-way sync of /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) to node2 via a root-owned cluster SSH keypair and a root cron job on node2 (*/5 * * * *) that pulls the file from node1 and replaces the local copy only when content differs — well under the 15-minute requirement. Verified end-to-end propagation of a real content change both before and after restarting each node. Also completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, rebooted node1 then node2 one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and verified services/data/crontab recovered on each before proceeding.
actions_performed: Verified root shell access and cluster networking on node1 and node2
Created /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source-of-truth file
Provisioned cluster SSH keypair on node2 and added the cluster public key to node1 root authorized_keys for passwordless node2->node1 SSH
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/sync-inventory-conf.sh on node2: pulls app.conf from node1 over SSH, replaces local file atomically only if content differs, logs via logger
Installed a root crontab entry on node2 (*/5 * * * *) running the sync script, logging to /var/log/sync-inventory-conf.log
Verified initial sync produced identical md5sum on both nodes
Modified node1's app.conf, confirmed divergence on node2, then observed the scheduled cron job (not a manual invocation) apply the change automatically with matching md5sum afterward
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, sshd/crond active, file md5sum) on both nodes

Rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (583ddd53...->5a81eb64...), and verified sshd active and file md5sum intact
Rebooted node2 the same way after node1 was confirmed healthy, confirmed boot_id changed (c2f29441...->3657304b...), and verified sshd/crond active, crontab intact, and file md5sum intact

Performed a second live change on node1 post-restart and confirmed the cron-driven sync on node2 still picked it up automatically at the next scheduled tick, proving the mechanism survived both restarts
